symptom: On mobile /prijzen, lifecycle routes and pricing sections visually fell apart and pricing controls were unreliable after repeated interaction fixes.
root_cause: A legacy page-wide @media(max-width:900px) rule converted every table, thead, tbody, tr, th and td on the pricing page into block/card layout. New lifecycle and M&A matrices were unintentionally captured by that global selector.
Two independent JavaScript controllers owned the same lifecycle, package-direction and billing controls, creating duplicate event handling and divergent state/update paths.
fix: Remove the obsolete page-wide mobile table-to-card transformation.
Keep matrices as native tables inside horizontal-scroll wrappers on narrow screens.
Remove the duplicate interaction guard and keep one canonical pricing controller.
Force hidden lifecycle panels and hidden plan cards to remain display:none on every viewport.
prevention: Never use unscoped element selectors such as table,thead,tbody,tr,th,td inside page-level responsive rules when multiple table components exist.
Each interactive control group must have one canonical state owner; do not layer fallback click controllers over an existing functional controller.
Pricing mobile regression tests must assert absence of global table-to-block CSS, presence of scroll wrappers, single-controller ownership and hidden-panel semantics.
evidence: prijzen.html contained the global mobile rule table,thead,tbody,tr,th,td{display:block;width:auto}.
prijzen.html simultaneously contained bg-pricing-neno-v1-js and bg-pricing-interaction-guard-v2 controlling the same pricing toggles.
PR #2666 removes both failure mechanisms and updates tests/brain-pricing-interactions-functional-v1.test.mjs.
